title: A linear one-parameter action with isolated fixed points on a general Borel quotient
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $B\subseteq G$ be a Borel subgroup, meaning a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]; solvable means that successive scheme-theoretic derived subgroups eventually become trivial, and the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. Let $Q$ be the $F$-scheme representing the fppf sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/B(A)$ on commutative $F$-algebras, for jointly surjective flat finitely presented coverings [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Give $Q$ the left $G$-action induced by multiplication on $G$. There exist a nonzero finite-dimensional $F$-vector space $E$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], a rational representation $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(E)$ (a homomorphism of $F$-group schemes, with $\operatorname{GL}(E)(A)=\operatorname{Aut}_A(E\otimes_F A)$), a $G$-equivariant closed immersion $i:Q\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(E)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-projective-morphism], and a homomorphism $\lambda:\mathbf G_{m,F}\to G$ [def-sc-gm-ga] for which the fixed subscheme $Q^{\lambda}$ is a finite nonempty disjoint union of reduced $F$-points. Here $\mathbf P(E)$ parametrizes one-dimensional subspaces; equivariance means $i(gx)=\rho(g)i(x)$ after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. The subscheme $Q^{\lambda}$ represents the functor whose $A$-points are those $x\in Q(A)$ such that $\lambda(t)x_{A^{\prime}}=x_{A^{\prime}}$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $A^{\prime}$ and every $t\in(A^{\prime})^\times$. A finite disjoint union of reduced $F$-points means an $F$-scheme isomorphic to $\coprod_{a=1}^r\operatorname{Spec}F$ for some integer $r\geq1$. The homomorphism $\lambda$ may be trivial, and $G=B$ is allowed. No reductivity hypothesis on $G$ is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 4.27, printed pp.94--95 (linear projective orbit); Theorem 17.9(a), p.354 (completeness), Section 17f, pp.368--369 (general flag variety), Lemma 17.52 and Proposition 17.53, p.369 (finite torus-fixed flags); Theorem 13.1, p.254 (smooth fixed subscheme), Lemma 13.51 and the paragraph preceding Proposition 13.52, pp.274--275 (separating cocharacter). Applied to the general connected group as in the proof of Theorem 17.65, p.374.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety] to obtain the smooth connected proper finite-type flag scheme $Y=\mathcal B(G)$ and $b_B\in Y(F)$, whose scheme stabilizer is $B$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry] its reduced orbit $O\subseteq Y$ is locally closed. It contains every $F$-point of $Y$, since the flag lemma says that $G(F)$ acts transitively on $Y(F)$. All closed points of $Y$ are $F$-rational by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], and they are dense by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space]. Thus the closure of $O$ is $Y$. The scheme $Y$ is reduced: smooth affine coordinate algebras over the reduced field $F$ are reduced by [lem-sfb-smooth-algebra-over-reduced-ring]. The locally closed reduced orbit with dense image is therefore open in $Y$. If its closed complement were nonempty, Jacobson density in that complement would give a closed point of $Y$ there, a contradiction. Hence $O=Y$; the reduced scheme structures agree because $Y$ is smooth and $O$ is its reduced orbit (the reduced induced structure on an open of a reduced scheme is the open subscheme structure). Now [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry] identifies $O$ with the represented fppf quotient $G/B=Q$, equivariantly by $gB\mapsto g b_B$. In particular $Q$ is nonempty, smooth, connected, proper and of finite type, and its rational points are labelled by the Borels, with the scheme-theoretic torus-fixed-point description of the flag lemma.

source.place: Section 17f, printed pp.368--369; Theorem 7.18, p.142. Closed-point argument: Stacks Tags 0478 and 00FV.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-scheme-line-stabilizer] with $H=B$. It gives $E\ne0$, $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(E)$ and a line $D\subseteq E$ with scheme stabilizer exactly $B$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry] the reduced orbit of $[D]$ in $\mathbf P(E)$ is locally closed. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry] it is canonically $G/B=Q$. Its inclusion therefore gives a $G$-equivariant immersion $i:Q\to\mathbf P(E)$, with $i(gB)=\rho(g)[D]$. The orbit isomorphism and the inclusion are morphisms of $G$-schemes, so this equality holds on every test algebra, including nonreduced algebras.

source.place: Theorem 4.27 and Remark 4.30, printed pp.94--96; Theorem 7.18, p.142; first paragraph of the proof of Theorem 17.65, p.374.

proof.text: Projective space is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated]. Since $Q$ is proper over $F$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] makes $i$ proper. An immersion is a monomorphism: open inclusions are monomorphisms, and on affine opens a closed immersion is induced by a surjective ring map, so a map into its source is uniquely determined by its composite [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Apply [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] to conclude that $i$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Theorem 17.65, p.374, projective embedding; Stacks Tags 01W6 (lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed) and 04XV (lemma-characterize-closed-immersion).

proof.text: Choose a maximal torus $T\subseteq B$, maximal in $G$, by [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy]; over $F$ it is a split torus, possibly of rank zero. By step 1 and [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety], the scheme-theoretically $T$-fixed rational points of $Q$ correspond exactly to the Borels $B'\supseteq T$. This set is nonempty because it contains $B$. By [lem-sfb-torus-normalizer-borel-transitivity] every such $B'$ is $nBn^{-1}$ for some $n\in N_G(T)(F)$. By [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-centralizer-borel], $C_G(T)(F)\subseteq B(F)$. Thus the map $n\mapsto nBn^{-1}$ is constant on right cosets of $C_G(T)(F)$: replacing $n$ by $nc$ gives $n(cBc^{-1})n^{-1}=nBn^{-1}$ since $c\in B(F)$. The quotient $N_G(T)(F)/C_G(T)(F)$ is finite by [lem-sfb-torus-normalizer-components]. Its surjection onto these Borels proves finiteness of the fixed rational-point set. No reductivity is used.

source.place: Corollary 17.11, printed p.355; Corollary 17.39(b), p.364; Lemma 17.52 and Proposition 17.53, p.369; finiteness of the Weyl group from Corollary 12.40, p.244.

proof.text: Fix a splitting $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ and restrict $\rho$ to $T$. Repeated application of [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] to its $r$ commuting factors gives a simultaneous weight basis of $E$. At each stage the remaining factors preserve each previous weight subspace, because their actions commute with that factor; decompose each such subspace for the next factor. After $r$ stages the scalar character on a simultaneous weight space is the product $t_1^{a_1}\cdots t_r^{a_r}$. Combine the spaces having the same exponent vector to obtain $E=\bigoplus_{\chi\in\Omega}E_\chi$ with pairwise distinct monomial characters and nonzero summands. For $r=0$ this is the single space $E$ with trivial character.

source.place: Theorem 12.12, printed pp.234--235; the decomposition used in Lemma 13.51, p.274.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-torus-fixed-weight-schemes] to this decomposition. It supplies $\lambda_T:\mathbf G_m\to T$ separating its characters. Put $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{\lambda_T}T\hookrightarrow G$. That lemma gives a closed subscheme $Z=\coprod_{\chi\in\Omega}\mathbf P(E_\chi)$ representing both ambient fixed functors. Since $i$ is equivariant and a closed immersion, its asserted pullback $H=Q\times_{\mathbf P(E)}Z$ represents both $Q^T$ and $Q^\lambda$, with exactly the universal quantifiers over algebra extensions in the item. The preimages $U_j=i^{-1}(D_+(z_j))$ of its eigenbasis charts are $T$-invariant affine opens covering $Q$: affineness follows from the quotient-ring characterization of a closed immersion in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The intersections $H\cap U_j$ represent $U_j^T$ and are closed in $U_j$.

source.place: Lemma 13.51 and the following paragraph, printed pp.274--275; fixed functor Theorem 7.1, pp.138--139.

proof.text: Every $U_j$ is smooth over $F$ by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], since it is open in the smooth scheme $Q$. It is affine of finite type: its coordinate algebra is a quotient of the polynomial coordinate algebra of the corresponding standard affine chart of $\mathbf P(E)$, since $i$ is closed. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-fixed-scheme-smooth] to $T,U_j$ and the represented closed fixed subscheme $H\cap U_j$. Each $H\cap U_j$ is smooth. Smoothness is local on the source, in the affine-local characterization of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], so their covering proves that $H$ is smooth over $F$. This applies also to the rank-zero torus and does not infer reducedness from a point count.

source.place: Theorem 13.1, printed p.254, applied on invariant affine eigenbasis charts; affine proof through Theorem 13.7, p.256.

proof.text: The closed subscheme $H\subseteq Q$ is of finite type over $F$: the finite family of affine charts from step 6 presents it by quotients of finitely generated polynomial algebras [def-weil-closed-immersion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] all its closed points have residue field $F$, so the set of closed points is exactly its finite, nonempty set $H(F)=Q^T(F)$ from step 4. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] these closed points are dense in $H$. Their finite union is already closed, hence equals $|H|$. Thus $|H|$ is a finite discrete space (each point is closed, and its complement is a finite union of closed points). In particular it has dimension zero.

source.place: Theorem 13.1 plus Lemma 17.52 and Proposition 17.53; Stacks varieties.tex Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson), algebra.tex Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz).

proof.text: Regard $H$ as its represented algebraic space [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. The scheme case of [lem-sfb-zero-dimensional-field-space-components] applies, by finite type and dimension zero from step 8. It writes $H$ as a disjoint union of open-and-closed one-point schemes $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$, with $A_a$ local Artinian and finite-dimensional over $F$. There are finitely many and at least one, by step 8. Smoothness of $H$ implies regularity of every local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. The local ring at the sole point of $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ is $A_a$ itself. It has dimension zero, so its maximal ideal is generated by zero elements by [def-weil-regular-scheme]; consequently that ideal is zero and $A_a$ is a field. Its residue field is $F$ by step 8, hence its structural map identifies $A_a$ with $F$. Therefore $Q^\lambda=H\simeq\coprod_{a=1}^s\operatorname{Spec}F$ for some $s\geq1$. Together with steps 2--3 this is all the asserted data and equivariance. If $G=B$, then $Q$ is a point and the construction allows a trivial cocharacter, as required.

source.place: Fixed-scheme smoothness: Theorem 13.1, p.254; Stacks varieties.tex Tags 056S (lemma-smooth-regular), 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0), and spaces-over-fields.tex Tag 06LZ (lemma-locally-finite-type-dim-zero); algebra.tex Tag 00KU (regular local rings).
